newsitem.title: INDIA: ARMY DEPLOYED TO KEEP PEACE IN INDIAN CITY.
newsitem.headline: ARMY DEPLOYED TO KEEP PEACE IN INDIAN CITY.

text.p: The government in India's northeastern state of Assam has called out army troops in the region's biggest city, Guwahati, to check separatist violence, a senior military officer said on Sunday.

The officer, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters the decision to deploy troops from Saturday night followed the killing of two senior army officers by the separatist guerrillas of the United Liberation Front of Asom (ULFA).
He did not say how many soldiers had been deployed.
On Friday two youths on a motor bike fired several rounds of bullets at the two officers opposite a newspaper office in Guwahati, eyewitnesses said.
The two gunmen fled the scene and both officers died in hospital.
There was no curfew but the military was helping state police maintain order and carrying out search operations.
The Maoist ULFA has been fighting since 1979 for a homeland in the oil-rich, tea-producing province, and accuses New Delhi of exploiting the state's forests and mineral resources.
